questions.question:
**Given below are six sentences, four of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives their connect order.**

Sentence 1. The British love chocolate.

P. In fact, they spend more on chocolate than any other European country!

Q. There is milk chocolate, dark chocolate and white chocolate.

R. If you go to any newsagent’s shop in the UK you’ll see a huge selection of chocolate bars on sale.

S. There are small bars of chocolate, medium-sized bars and massive bars of chocolate.

Sentence 6. You can buy mint-flavoured chocolate, chocolate-covered peanuts or raisins, chocolate with nuts, chocolate with toffee … the list is endless!
questions.solution:
P is considered the second sentence as it supports the love for chocolate that the British have (first sentence).

Q and S list the various kinds of chocolates whereas R introduces the huge variety of chocolate bars.

So, R comes before Q and S.

The correct order of sentences will be **PRQS. **Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the passive form of the sentence given below:**

I don’t think a child can do this mischief.

options.text: I don’t think this mischief can be done by a child.
I don’t think a child could have done this mischief.
I don’t think this mischief was done by a child.
I don’t think this mischief could have been done by a child.

questions.solution:
Here, we need to express “a child can do this mischief” in the passive form.

**Tense remains the same.**

__Switching subject and object __ > *a child can do this mischief *turns into* this mischief can be done by a child*

In the rest of the sentence “I don’t think’ remains unchanged.

Hence, the passive form of the sentence will be **option 1.**

*I don’t think this mischief can be done by a child.*

questions.question: Which of the following words should be filled at (1) as per context of the passage from the given options?
questions.solution:
People can **plan **a vacation, but not an earthquake. Also, no one knows what can happen at the next moment. So, no one can **state** about an earthquake.

**Guess **is to say something without any related information.

One can say anything about an earthquake only on the basis of some information available. So, one can only **predict **an earthquake.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following words should be filled at (2) as per context of the passage from the given options?
questions.solution:
The phrase ‘little damage’ means negligible or very less damage. So, little damage implies that the earthquake has no effect on anyone.

‘**Barely**’ means negligible or almost not existing and is hence the correct fit for this blank.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following words should be filled at (3) as per context of the passage from the given options?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Extensive'.**

questions.question:
**Select the word which is closest in meaning to the word in capitals.**

INDUCE
questions.solution:
**Forbid **and **caution **mean exactly opposite of the word ‘**induce**’ which means to succeed in persuading or leading (someone) to do something.

**Compel **is to force. For eg:

*Some parents **compel** their kids to study hard.*

**Coax, **on the other hand,** **is to gently persuade someone to do something.

For eg: *She **coaxed** her husband to buy her a new necklace.*

It is clearly similar in meaning to the word **induce **and is hence the correct answer.

questions.question:
‘If you dry off the sanitizer before it evaporates all the way, you’re actually reducing its effectiveness.

Here, ‘its effectiveness’ refers to the ability
questions.solution:
‘**Effectiveness**’ is the ability to produce a wanted or intended result.

Here, our wanted result is “to kill germs” using the sanitizer.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: The effectiveness of the sanitizer depends on

options.text: The content of soap in them

questions.solution:
The part of the passage *“They only work, however, if they have enough alcohol to kill the germs—at least 60 percent”* clearly states that sanitizers are effective based on the ***alcohol content*** in them.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
Which word in the text has the following meaning?

Continuing to exist or occur for a long period of time
questions.solution:
‘**Persistent**’ is the only word that is present in the passage with the meaning ‘continuing to exist or occur for a long period of time’.

**Perpetual**, **continuous **and **never ending **mean the same thing, ie. occurring repeatedly; so frequent as to seem endless and uninterrupted.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question: The intention of the text is NOT to:

options.text: examine the advantages of using sanitizers
caution against the use of sanitizers

questions.solution:
It is clear that the passage explains why doctors use sanitizers, examines the advantages of using sanitizers, cautions against the use of sanitizers. But there is no mention about promoting the use of sanitizers.

The passage is clearly not a marketing advertisement. Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: Why do doctors use hand sanitizers rather than soap and water?
questions.solution:
The passage states that "As doctors and nurses are often rushed in their daily activities, hand sanitizers can really come in handy."

This means that doctors use hand sanitizers because they are easier to use.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the word which is opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.**

FUSION
questions.solution:
**Fusion** is a process of joining or combining two or more into one. **Separation** is exactly the opposite process and is hence its antonym.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

**Disintegration **means the process of coming to pieces. Fusion and **combination **are synonyms. 

**Distribution **is the process in which something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.**

Rahul is **__a great hand__ **at organizing parties.
questions.solution:
Let us look at the example:

*Sachin Tendulkar is **a great hand** at batting.* This idiom conveys the meaning that he is very proficient at the activity of batting.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate word to complete the sentence.**

She became _______ for her commitment to democracy.
questions.solution:
The word in the blank should be an **adjective **as it says something about the subject ‘**she**’.

‘**Popular**’ is an adjective while all the other options are nouns.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment of the sentence given below that contains a grammatical error.**

A chips-marketing company held a competition recently for find new exciting flavours for their potato chips.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is __**for find**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **'for finding' **should be there in place of **'for find'**
 
• We use ‘**for + verb-ing**’ to **talk about the function of an object**. It’s used when we want to explain what something is generally used for or what its purpose is. **We DON’T use ‘for + infinitive’.**
 
 
• A camera is for taking photos. (NOT: 'for take' photos.)
 
• The headphones are for listening to music. 
 
• This knife is for chopping onions.
 
 

**The correct sentence is: ***A chips-marketing company held a competition recently **for finding** new exciting flavours for their potato chips.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When the subject of the sentence is a person, and we are talking about the function of an object, it’s also possible to use ‘to + infinitive’, as well as ‘for + verb-ing’.**

 
 
• I use this box to store DVDs.
 
• I use this box for storing DVDs.

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate word to complete the sentence.**

A committee had _______ agreed to back the bill on GST.
questions.solution:
A **committee **is itself a group of people. People in the committee are together and united already and take decisions in a concerted ie. coordinated way. So, there is no need to mention these adverbs. Also, the word ‘unitedly’ does not exist in the language.

‘**Unanimously**’ means with the agreement of all people and without any opposition and is the correct fit for the sentence.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the passive form of the sentence given below.**

She bakes an apple pie for Jane every Sunday.

options.text: An apple pie was being baked by her for Jane every Sunday.
An apple pie is being baked by her for Jane every Sunday.
An apple pie is baked by her for Jane every Sunday.
An apple pie was baked by her for Jane every Sunday.

questions.solution:
**Let us remember that tense remains the same** in both active and passive forms.

Therefore:

**bakes **in active form → **is baked **in passive form (simple present tense)

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct form of reported speech of the sentence given below.**

“Who will complete the work?” asked the shoemaker.

options.text: The shoemaker said I wonder who will complete the work.
The shoemaker said who will complete the work.
The shoemaker asked who would complete the work.
The shoemaker asked who will complete the work.

questions.solution:
The phrase “asked the shoemaker” is in **simple past** tense. So, the sentence in quotes should be converted to appropriate past tense.

**Who will complete → who would complete**

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.**

A raised place on which offerings are made to God.
questions.solution:
**Shrine**: a worship place. Eg: Shrine of Kedarnath.

**Temple**: a building used for worship. Eg: Shiv temple

**Pilgrimage**: a journey to a holy place

**Altar**: a table or a raised to make offerings

Therefore, we can see that the word we are looking for is **altar **ie. **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

There ______ news tonight.
questions.solution:
The word ‘**news**’ is a singular noun. So, a singular verb should be used.

The verb ‘has’ means to own or possess. So, in this context, it is correct to use ‘**is**’.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

The correct sentence will be: *There **is not much** news tonight.*

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate word to complete the sentence.**

He played down his ______ of becoming chairman.
questions.solution:
‘To play down the **possibility **of something’ means to try to make something seem less likely than it might actually be.

In this context, the subject is trying to make it seem less possible that he might become the chairman.

None of the other words convey this meaning.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate word to complete the sentence.**

___________ by his arrogant and reckless behavior, the employer sacked him.
questions.solution:
One can get very angry with someone’s arrogant or reckless behavior, but not excited or tired.

**Incensed **means ‘very angry’. Also, ‘by’ is not a preposition that can be used with ‘angry’.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: **Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.**

options.text: I have no idea whom should I speak to about this problem.
I have no idea to whom should I speak to about this problem.
I have no idea to whom I should speak to about this problem.
I have no idea whom I should speak to about this problem.

questions.solution:
“Whom should I speak to?” is a question. A question cannot be present in a simple sentence the way it has been placed in options 1 and 2.

It should be changed to “**whom I should speak to**” to be included in a simple sentence. 

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the sentence that is in indirect speech below.**

The boy pleaded with the teacher not to call his parents to school.

options.text: The boy said to the teacher, “Please don’t call my parents to school.”
The boy warned the teacher, “Don’t call my parents to school.”
The boy told the teacher, “Don’t call my parents to school.”
The boy pleaded, “The teacher should not call my parents to school.”

questions.solution:
The verb **pleaded **indicates request in indirect→ Use the word **“please..” **in direct speech. This is missing in all other sentences.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Options 2 and 4 imply that the boy was warning the teacher and are hence incorrect.
